_meta.description: Live macro themes affecting currencies but not on the scheduled news calendar. Update as regime-changing events happen. Scanner reads this at brief generation time and displays it in the daily/weekly review.
_meta.howToUse: Each theme should include: (1) short title, (2) start date, (3) currency implications with brief reasoning, (4) a specific watchLevel that would invalidate the theme, (5) affectedPairs for scanner correlation. Retire themes by moving to _retired[] with an endDate.

themes.title: Canada-US trade war live — Sep 8 retaliation in effect, Trump federal-contracts ban added; oil above $100 capping USDCAD; Jan 1 2027 50% auto tariff threat structural; BoC Oct 28 next binary
themes.summary: As of September 13, the Canada-US trade war is structurally unchanged from the Sep 8-9 escalation peak but a new commodity variable has emerged. Canada's C$27.6 billion, 700+ tariff-line retaliatory package — rates of 15%, 25%, and 50% matched dollar-for-dollar to US Section 338 and Section 232 tariffs, including doubling steel and aluminum duties to 50% — remains live since 12:01 a.m. September 8. Trump's Sep 8 evening counter-escalation directing federal agencies to bar Canadian-origin products from government contracts remains unrevoked and no diplomatic channel has been opened. The key market development since Sep 9 is oil: WTI crude has crossed above $100/barrel (cited in multiple September 10-11 sources) driven by ongoing US-Iran military hostilities disrupting Strait of Hormuz traffic. Oil above $100 is a material CAD tailwind via Canada's energy export channel that is actively suppressing USDCAD and preventing the pair from reaching the 1.39-1.40 targets that the tariff-war USD bid alone would imply. USDCAD is currently trading near 1.3837 — up from the Sep 8 low of 1.3783 but well below the 1.3900 resistance level, as oil above $100 is offsetting tariff-war CAD negativity almost exactly. Canadian August employment printed -41,700 (vs +15,000 expected), signaling real tariff damage to the labor market. The Bank of Canada held at 2.25% on September 2 with a hawkish inflation tilt acknowledging tariff pass-through risks while flagging growth uncertainty — a stance that limits BoC easing expectations from crushing CAD further. The structural Jan 1, 2027 threat of 50% tariffs on all Canadian autos, trucks, parts, and steel remains the medium-term CAD overhang. No diplomatic off-ramp is visible: both governments have publicly committed to their retaliatory frameworks and the Trump administration has added non-tariff escalation levers. The US-Iran conflict and its effect on oil is now the primary short-term USDCAD swing variable, with trade-war direction determining the medium-term trend.

implications.CAD: MAXIMUM structural CAD negative from tariff war — US Section 338 50% tariffs live since Aug 22, Canada 700+ line dollar-for-dollar retaliation live since Sep 8, Trump federal-contracts ban Sep 8 evening, zero diplomatic off-ramp, Jan 1 2027 50% auto tariff threat. However oil above $100 (US-Iran, Hormuz) is a powerful commodity tailwind actively capping USDCAD at ~1.3837. Net directional bias remains USDCAD long on any oil pullback from $100+. BoC Oct 28 is the next policy binary — held 2.25% Sep 2 with hawkish tilt but labor market deteriorating (-41,700 Aug jobs).
implications.USD: USDCAD directionally bullish on tariff war fundamentals but oil above $100 is a meaningful offset. Hot Aug CPI (core +0.3% MoM) has also strengthened USD broadly — dual tailwind for USDCAD upside if oil retreats from $100+.
implications.MXN: USMCA credibility damage from US-Canada rupture keeps uncertainty elevated for Mexico. Divergence in US-Mexico vs US-Canada bilateral progress adds structural uncertainty premium to MXN.
implications.EUR: Indirect — EURCAD likely bid on structural CAD weakness. Broader protectionism signal from Section 338 invocation has limited but non-zero EUR contagion via global trade uncertainty.
implications.AUD: Commodity-bloc — AUD partially insulated by elevated oil and copper prices but trades defensively in acute CAD-shock episodes. AUDUSD supported by oil/commodity complex but subject to tariff-war risk-off and USD strength from hot CPI.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDCAD vol elevated. NZD defensive in commodity-bloc risk-off episodes triggered by tariff escalation.
implications.GBP: GBPCAD directional trade on CAD structural weakness. GBP otherwise dominated by BoE path and USD dynamics from FOMC.
implications.JPY: CADJPY under dual pressure — CAD structural weakness from Section 338 tariff war plus JPY structural bid from BOJ Sep 17-18 hike (100% economist consensus per Bloomberg survey).

themes.watchLevel: USDCAD ~1.3837 as of Sep 13 — oil above $100 (US-Iran) is the dominant short-term swing factor. Key upside: 1.3900 is the critical resistance — a clean daily close above 1.3900 opens 1.4017-1.4100 and requires oil to pull back below $95 meaningfully. Theme ends only on: (1) formal re-opening of US-Canada talks with credible framework, or (2) Trump executive action suspending Section 338.

themes.title: USDJPY ~157.90 — CPI USD squeeze from 154.60 low; BOJ Sep 17-18 hike NOW 100% economist consensus (all 52 Bloomberg forecasters); Reuters confirms 25bp to 1.25%; dual central bank week FOMC Sep 15 → BOJ Sep 18 is live
themes.summary: As of September 13, the BOJ September 17-18 hike narrative has hardened from 84% market pricing to 100% economist consensus. A Bloomberg survey of all 52 BOJ watchers published September 11 shows every single forecaster expects the Bank of Japan to raise its benchmark rate at the September 18 meeting, with 93% anticipating a follow-up hike by January and approximately one-third predicting December. Reuters has separately confirmed the BOJ is set to hike by 25 basis points next week. The current BOJ policy rate is 1.00% (held since July 31, 2026 decision); a September hike would bring it to 1.25%. The critical development since the Sep 9 update is that USDJPY has partially reversed its collapse: the pair bounced from the September 8 intraday low of approximately 154.56-154.60 to approximately 157.90 as of September 13, as the hot August CPI print on September 11 (core +0.3% MoM, a tick above the 0.2% consensus; headline 3.4% YoY) triggered a sharp USD short-squeeze that lifted USDJPY roughly 330 pips off the lows. This move is consistent with the prior watchLevel scenario — 'hot CPI: USDJPY bounces to 156-157 temporarily before BOJ meeting' — though the bounce has extended slightly further to ~157.90 as FOMC hike odds moved toward ~70%. The intervention regime credibility at 160.00 remains fully intact: the pair has not recovered above 158 and the MoF/BOJ have not disclaimed further intervention. The dual central bank binary week is now two days away: the FOMC announces September 15-16 (decision September 16) followed by the BOJ September 17-18. A scenario in which the FOMC hikes to 3.75-4.00% and the BOJ hikes to 1.25% within 48 hours remains the maximum two-way USDJPY volatility scenario: initial USDJPY rally on FOMC USD bid, then sharp and likely larger JPY surge on BOJ confirmation. Governor Ueda's September 2 G20 Asheville signal and board member Takata's Sapporo comments both remain on record as hawkish pre-commitments. The Bessent-Ueda bilateral at G20 confirming US-Japan policy coordination is structurally intact.

implications.JPY: BOJ Sep 17-18 hike to 1.25% is NOW 100% economist consensus (all 52 Bloomberg forecasters), Reuters-confirmed. USDJPY bounced from 154.60 to ~157.90 on hot Aug CPI USD short-squeeze — but the BOJ binary in 5 days is the dominant driver. If FOMC hikes Sep 16 (now ~70% odds post-CPI), USDJPY may temporarily spike before BOJ overwhelms the move. BOJ hike confirmed = USDJPY likely drops sharply toward 153-150, extending the structural JPY bull trend. 2yr JGB yields at multi-decade highs. Intervention regime at 160.00 intact.
implications.USD: USDJPY has partially recovered to ~157.90 from 154.60 low on hot Aug CPI (core +0.3% MoM). FOMC Sep 15-16 hike (~70% priced post-CPI) is the near-term USD catalyst but the rate differential direction of travel is decisively USD-negative vs JPY as BOJ accelerates normalization. Medium-term USDJPY trajectory is lower.

implications.GBP: GBPJPY under intervention regime and carry-unwind pressure — Sep 8 JPY surge hit all crosses; partial recovery since on CPI USD bid but BOJ Sep 18 is the next directional catalyst.
implications.CHF: CHFJPY lower on intervention pressure and BOJ normalization cycle. SNB in easing mode adds divergence.
implications.CAD: CADJPY lower on dual pressure — CAD structural weakness from Section 338 tariff war plus JPY structural bid from BOJ 100% consensus hike.

implications.NZD: Same dynamic as AUD. NZDJPY under intervention and carry-unwind pressure. BOJ Sep 18 binary dominant.

themes.watchLevel: USDJPY ~157.90 as of Sep 13 — bounced ~330 pips from 154.60 Sep 8 low on hot CPI USD short-squeeze. Key resistance: 158.00-158.50 (psychological and prior technical support-turned-resistance); a clean move above 158.50 toward 160.00 before the BOJ meeting would represent carry traders fully re-engaging and would require MoF/Bessent intervention disclaimer. Key support: 156.50 (round number and prior range); 155.00 is the next major support; 154.56 (Sep 8 intraday low) is the critical floor. FOMC Sep 15-16 binary (now ~70% hike priced): hike = USDJPY spike toward 159-160 temporarily, then likely violent reversal on BOJ; hold = USDJPY drops back toward 155-156, BOJ hike then accelerates JPY strength toward 153-150. BOJ Sep 17-18 hard binary: hike to 1.25% (100% consensus) = USDJPY drops toward 153-150, 2yr JGB yields spike; shock no-hike = USDJPY violent rally to 160+, intervention regime faces maximum stress. USDJPY above 160.00 = intervention regime invalidated and theme re-characterization required. USDJPY below 153.00 = BOJ hike confirmed and structural JPY bull trend extended to next leg.

themes.title: FOMC Sep 15-16 NOW 2 DAYS AWAY — Aug CPI Sep 11 resolved hawkishly (core +0.3% MoM above 0.2% consensus, headline 3.4%); hike odds ~70%; Warsh SEP/dot plot binary imminent; dual CB week with BOJ Sep 17-18
themes.summary: As of September 13, the September 11 August CPI report has resolved the pre-FOMC tiebreaker in the hawkish direction, and the FOMC meeting on September 15-16 is now just two days away. The August CPI printed: headline +0.4% MoM (in-line with Bloomberg consensus), 3.4% YoY (unchanged from July); core CPI +0.3% MoM — a tick above the 0.2% forecast — with the annual core rate easing to 2.4% (the lowest since March 2021). Energy drove the headline, with gasoline up 3.9% MoM and overall fuel costs up 28% year-over-year; oil has now crossed above $100/barrel as of September 10-11 on US-Iran Hormuz disruption, adding a structural supply-side inflation upside risk that was not present in the prior update. The hot core print — coming after August payrolls of +162,000 (approximately three times consensus) — has pushed FOMC hike odds to approximately 70% per post-CPI market pricing (US News September 11), with some sources citing CME FedWatch at 80-90%. This is a material shift from the 54% hold / 46% hike split on Kalshi as of September 9. Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole framework — PCE at 3.7%, 6-month PCE at 4.1%, financial conditions 'not broadly restrictive,' 'work to do' on inflation — is now fully validated by the August data. The July FOMC vote was 9-3 to hold with three regional bank presidents (Cleveland, Minneapolis, Dallas) all dissenting for a hike — the most dissents since September 2016. The September 15-16 FOMC will produce an updated Summary of Economic Projections and dot plot; if the FOMC hikes to 3.75-4.00% with a dot plot showing the 2026 median at 4.00%+, this represents the full hawkish validation of the Warsh regime. The dual central bank binary is now imminent: FOMC September 16 decision → BOJ September 18 decision, within 48 hours. A simultaneous-tightening scenario in which both central banks hike within 48 hours remains the maximum FX volatility event of 2026 — initial USDJPY rally on FOMC USD bid, then sharp JPY surge on BOJ confirmation.

implications.USD: DXY has strengthened post-hot-CPI. FOMC Sep 15-16 hike (~70% priced) is the near-term binary: hike 25bps to 3.75-4.00% with hawkish dots (2026 median 4.00%+) = full validation, DXY targets 101-102, EURUSD below 1.1300; hold with hawkish dots = partial validation, USD dips then recovers; hold with unchanged dots = sell-the-news USD weakness, DXY retraces to 98.50-99.00. 10yr UST near 4.79% — sustained move above 4.85% = Dec hike being priced. Oil above $100 is an upside inflation wildcard keeping the hike case structurally supported.
implications.JPY: Hot Aug CPI triggered USDJPY short-squeeze from 154.60 to ~157.90 — the 'hot CPI = USDJPY bounce to 156-157' watchLevel scenario was realized and extended. FOMC Sep 16 hike (now ~70% priced) could push USDJPY temporarily toward 159-160 before BOJ Sep 18 overwhelms the move. The dual-hike 48-hour scenario (FOMC + BOJ) is the maximum two-way volatility event.

Hike to 3.75-4.00% with hawkish dots = EURUSD toward 1.1300-1.1350; hold with hawkish dots = relief bounce to 1.1600+.
implications.GBP: GBPUSD ~1.3489 (per Yahoo Sep 13) — subject to FOMC outcome and post-Warsh USD strength. BoE's own path is an independent GBP driver but FOMC dominates near-term.
implications.CAD: Hot CPI + FOMC hike odds ~70% add a second USD tailwind to USDCAD alongside Section 338 tariff structural bid. USDCAD at 1.3837 — oil above $100 is the primary offset preventing a move toward 1.40. Sep 15-16 FOMC is a dual USDCAD catalyst.
implications.AUD: AUDUSD ~0.7062 (per Yahoo Sep 13). Hot CPI has already pressured AUD lower from recent highs. FOMC hike scenario = AUDUSD lower toward 0.69-0.70; hold = AUD relief. Oil above $100 provides partial commodity support.
implications.NZD: NZDUSD ~0.5886 (per Yahoo Sep 13). Same as AUD — FOMC Sep 16 dominant near-term binary. RBNZ dynamics provide independent NZD input.
implications.CHF: USDCHF ~0.8018 per cross-rates. Lifted by Warsh hawkish repricing and hot CPI. SNB easing mode limits CHF upside. CHF safe-haven bid provides partial offset in risk-off scenarios.

themes.watchLevel: FOMC Sep 15-16 is the hard binary — decision September 16 (2 days away). Hike 25bps to 3.75-4.00% with hawkish SEP (2026 dot median 4.00%+): full validation, DXY targets 101-102, EURUSD below 1.1300, USDJPY spikes toward 159-160 before BOJ overwhelms; hold with hawkish dots (2026 median above 4.00%): partial validation, USD dips then stabilizes, EURUSD 1.1500-1.1550; hold with unchanged dots: sell-the-news USD weakness, DXY retraces toward 98.50-99.00, EURUSD toward 1.1700+. FOMC Sep 16 arrives 48hrs before BOJ Sep 18 (100% economist consensus hike) — simultaneous-tightening scenario is the maximum USDJPY volatility event of 2026. 10yr UST at 4.79% key level — sustained above 4.85% = Dec hike being priced. Oil above $100 (US-Iran, Hormuz) is the structural upside inflation wildcard that keeps the hike case alive. DXY sustaining below 98.00 post-FOMC = Warsh hawkish theme fully unwound. Theme retires: post-Sep 16 FOMC decision with updated SEP resolves this binary; replaced by post-FOMC regime assessment at next update.
